title: Finite-free relative tensor coordinates and normalized unitors
statement:
Let $C$ be an essentially small site, and let $H=\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Ab})$ have the canonical sheafified tensor over $\mathbf Z$, with sheafification and closed symmetric monoidal structure as in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Use internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and the coequalizer relative tensor and its induced monoidal structure [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. For any commutative ring object $R$, write $U:\operatorname{Mod}_R(H)\to H$ for the forgetful functor and $t_{P,M}:UP\otimes UM\to U(P\otimes_R M)$ for the canonical coequalizer projection.
Let $R$ be a commutative ring object of $H$, let $N$ be an $R$-module, let $n\geq0$ be an integer, and let $\theta:R^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ be an $R$-module isomorphism. Here $R^{\oplus n}$ is the finite biproduct of regular modules, with inclusions $\iota_i$ and projections $\pi_i$; put $e_i=\theta\iota_i:R\to N$ and $q_i=\pi_i\theta^{-1}:N\to R$. Write $\rho_i:M^n\to M$ for the finite-product projections, $L_M:R\otimes_R M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ for the left unitor of the relative module tensor, $\lambda_{UM}:\mathbf1\otimes UM\xrightarrow{\sim}UM$ for the ambient left unitor, $\eta_R:\mathbf1\to R$ for the ring unit, and $\gamma_M:R\otimes UM\to UM$ for the action. The induced relative unitor has the following normalization in $H$:
$$U(L_M)\circ t_{R,M}=\gamma_M,\qquad U(L_M^{-1})=t_{R,M}\circ(\eta_R\otimes\operatorname{id}_{UM})\circ\lambda_{UM}^{-1}.$$
There is a natural isomorphism of $R$-module valued functors
$$D_\theta:N\otimes_R-\xrightarrow{\sim}(-)^n$$
with the following identities in $\operatorname{Mod}_R(H)$:
$$\rho_iD_{\theta,M}=L_M\circ(q_i\otimes_R\operatorname{id}_M),\qquad D_{\theta,M}^{-1}=\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)}(e_i\otimes_R\operatorname{id}_M)\circ L_M^{-1}\circ\rho_i.$$
On underlying sheaves these identities are normalized by the canonical coequalizer projections:
$$U(\rho_iD_{\theta,M})\circ t_{N,M}=\gamma_M\circ(Uq_i\otimes\operatorname{id}_{UM}),$$
$$U(D_{\theta,M}^{-1})=\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)}t_{N,M}\circ((Ue_i\circ\eta_R)\otimes\operatorname{id}_{UM})\circ\lambda_{UM}^{-1}\circ U\rho_i.$$
For every $R$-linear map $f:M\to M'$ the naturality equation is
$$D_{\theta,M'}\circ(\operatorname{id}_N\otimes_R f)=f^n\circ D_{\theta,M}.$$
All assertions include $n=0$, with empty biproduct, empty product and empty sums. The statements concern the canonical sheaf tensor and relative tensor; they do not identify sections of a tensor sheaf with sectionwise tensors.

proof.text: The module left unitor is induced from the bimodule left unitor. Expand its forward map as the tensor of the regular-bimodule comparison followed by the action-induced coequalizer descent. Naturality of the coequalizer projection, the identity underlying the regular comparison, and coequalizer.pi_desc give t_(R,M) followed by U(L_M) equal to the action. To compute U(L_M inverse), cancel the monomorphism U(L_M); the forward formula and the module unit axiom show that unit insertion followed by t_(R,M) has composite identity. This proves both unitor normalizations.

proof.text: In any preadditive monoidal category with finite biproducts and additive tensor, construct the component isomorphism by tensoring theta inverse, applying Mathlib rightDistributor to the finite family of tensor units, applying the biproduct of left unitors, then applying biproduct.isoProduct. Specialize this construction to the internal module category with its existing relative tensor.

proof.text: The rightDistributor projection formula, biproduct.mapIso projection formula and biproduct.isoProduct_hom give D_M followed by rho_i equal to (q_i tensor identity) followed by L_M. Expand the inverse using rightDistributor_inv and biproduct.isoProduct_inv. Distribute composition over the finite sum and use biproduct projection identities to obtain exactly the sum of rho_i followed by L_M inverse followed by (e_i tensor identity). These Mathlib isomorphisms and identities hold for the empty finite family as well.

proof.text: Precompose the forward coordinate formula with t_(N,M), apply Mod.tensorObjpi_whiskerRight and the first unitor normalization. This gives the forward underlying-sheaf equation. Apply the additive forgetful functor to the inverse coordinate sum, use the inverse unitor normalization in each summand, commute each basis inclusion past the coequalizer projection by the same tensorObjpi naturality, and combine successive right whiskerings. This gives exactly the stated inverse underlying-sheaf sum.

proof.text: For a module map f, check naturality of the component maps after every finite-product projection. Substitute the forward coordinate equation and Pi.map_pi, then use naturality of the left unitor and whisker exchange. Assemble the component isomorphisms with NatIso.ofComponents. Its naturality equation is the last clause of the theorem. Every construction and every finite-sum computation includes n=0; no nonempty or positive-rank hypothesis is used.

Source: main-20261015 lem-sfb-subfield-flat proof, last sentence: 'F_X⊗_{E_X}M≅M^n naturally'. The item makes this inference precise for its parent lem-sfb-finite-free-scalar-coordinates. Step checks: (1) sheafification is additive by the uniqueness in def-weil-pbc-sheafification, so the tensor and Mod_R are additive. (2) Finite products of modules carry the action γ_{M_i}(1⊗ρ_i); the unit and associativity laws follow from naturality of λ and α, the j_i make the product a biproduct, and q_ie_j=δ, Σe_iq_i=1. (3) t is epi, and U(a⊗_R b)t = t(Ua⊗Ub) as the induced map on coequalizers; tensor additivity follows by cancelling t, then faithfulness of U. (4) The unitor is action-induced by lem-sfb-bimod-monoidal; the regular module's symmetric right action is μβ=μ, so the bimodule and relative coequalizers coincide; U(L)v=γ(η⊗1)λ⁻¹=1 gives the formula for the inverse. (5) A_iB_j=δ_ij, SD=(Σe_iq_i)⊗1=1, and DS=1 by projections. (6) The underlying-sheaf formulas match the statement exactly. (7) Naturality follows from naturality of L; for n=0, 1_N=0. Edge cases checked: n=0, n=1, R=0, M=0. proof_deps equals the union of step uses. Accepted tool use: lem-sfb-bimod-monoidal, a Mathlib leaf (Bimod.monBicategory). Duplicate search: lem-sfb-balanced-tensor-finite-free-comparison (NI, unsplit) has the free module in the right variable and a coproduct target, so it is not a duplicate (advisory); lem-sfb-ringed-site-free-matrix-scalar-extension is a different statement. Minor point: step 3's induced morphism action is literally stated in lem-sfb-bimod-monoidal, which step 3 does not cite, but deriving it from the coequalizer is elementary.

lean.statement: theorem sfb_relative_tensor_finite_free_coordinates (N : Mod (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w}) R) (n : ℕ) (θ : (⨁ fun _ : Fin n ↦ Mod.regular R) ≅ N) : (∀ M : Mod (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w}) R, Mod.tensorObjπ (Mod.regular R) M ≫ (λ_ M).hom.hom = γ[R,M.X] ∧ (λ_ M).inv.hom = (λ_ M.X).inv ≫ η[R] ▷ M.X ≫ Mod.tensorObjπ (Mod.regular R) M) ∧ ∃ D : tensorLeft N ≅ Functor.pi' (fun _ : Fin n ↦ 𝟭 (Mod (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w}) R)) ⋙ Limits.Pi.functor (Fin n), (∀ (M : Mod (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w}) R) (i : Fin n), (D.app M).hom ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n ↦ M) i = ((θ.inv ≫ biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin n ↦ Mod.regular R) i) ▷ M) ≫ (λ_ M).hom) ∧ (∀ M : Mod (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w}) R, (D.app M).inv = ∑ i : Fin n, Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n ↦ M) i ≫ (λ_ M).inv ≫ ((biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n ↦ Mod.regular R) i ≫ θ.hom) ▷ M)) ∧ (∀ (M : Mod (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w}) R) (i : Fin n), Mod.tensorObjπ N M ≫ ((D.app M).hom ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n ↦ M) i).hom = (θ.inv ≫ biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin n ↦ Mod.regular R) i).hom ▷ M.X ≫ γ[R,M.X]) ∧ (∀ M : Mod (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w}) R, (D.app M).inv.hom = ∑ i : Fin n, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n ↦ M) i).hom ≫ (λ_ M.X).inv ≫ (η[R] ≫ (biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n ↦ Mod.regular R) i ≫ θ.hom).hom) ▷ M.X ≫ Mod.tensorObjπ N M) ∧ (∀ (M M' : Mod (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w}) R) (f : M ⟶ M'), (N ◁ f) ≫ (D.app M').hom = (D.app M).hom ≫ Limits.Pi.map (fun _ : Fin n ↦ f))
